sections.title: 2026 US Inflation Snapshot: CPI Trend and Consumer Impact
sections.content: Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose from 320.62 in January 2025 to 333.979 in May 2026, marking a 4.17% year-over-year increase. This upward trend reflects persistent inflationary pressures, though the pace has moderated compared to prior years. Real disposable personal income grew by 1.7% in 2025 but shows signs of deceleration, while personal consumption expenditures continue to rise steadily, indicating resilient consumer spending despite economic headwinds.

data.title: Pricing Sensitivity in Discretionary Sectors
data.evidence: Consumer sentiment at 44.8 (May 2026) signals heightened price sensitivity, particularly in apparel and electronics where demand remains elastic despite inflation.

data.title: Housing Market Lag Impacting Furniture Demand
data.evidence: Housing starts declined 15% YoY (May 2026), while building materials retail sales rose 4.5%, suggesting deferred discretionary spending on home furnishings.

data.title: Stable Employment Supports Gradual Spending
data.evidence: Unemployment remained stable at ~4.3%, supporting steady personal consumption expenditures despite low consumer confidence.

data.title: Mixed Sector Performance Reflects Inflation Resilience
data.evidence: Furniture and electronics show mixed performance with bearish outliers (e.g., Ethan Allen, GoPro), while apparel brands like Columbia Sportswear demonstrate resilience.
